calendar.description: Latest monthly activity; compare like-for-like growth periods.

CPI and RPI outturn; their fiscal channels and indexation lags differ.

calendar.description: Bank Rate decision and minutes, scheduled for 12 noon UK time.
New borrowing observation plus annual revisions and classification updates.

Revised activity and nominal GDP information can alter fiscal ratios.

undatedWatch.event: Next OBR Economic and fiscal outlook
undatedWatch.description: The OBR publications page specifies the season; no exact date is asserted here.

events.event: Growth plan and future investment funding announced
events.description: HM Treasury announced City Investment Funds and a Cambridge loans package, stating that new funding would be scored at Autumn Budget 2026. An announcement is not an OBR-certified fiscal costing.
events.likelyFiscalChannel: Public investment and financial transactions; the borrowing effect depends on the final policy specification and accounting treatment.

events.event: OBR published its long-term fiscal risk assessment
events.description: The 2026 Fiscal risks and sustainability report examines pressures over the next 50 years. These conditional long-run projections are distinct from the March medium-term forecast.
events.likelyFiscalChannel: Demography, productivity and long-run spending and receipts assumptions affect debt sustainability beyond the fiscal-rule horizon.

events.description: The MPC voted 6–3 to maintain Bank Rate at 3.75%; three members preferred a quarter-point increase.
events.likelyFiscalChannel: Short-term public financing costs and reserve remuneration; longer gilt yields also depend on the expected future path of rates and risk premia.

events.event: GDP grew 0.4% in the three months to June
events.description: ONS estimated real GDP growth of 0.4% in April–June compared with January–March 2026. This quarterly growth rate is not directly comparable with annual OBR growth assumptions.
events.likelyFiscalChannel: Activity affects tax bases; nominal GDP also affects fiscal ratios. A real quarterly growth observation alone does not quantify either fiscal effect.

events.description: Annual CPI inflation increased from 2.6% in June to 2.9% in July 2026. Housing and household services contributed to the increase.
events.likelyFiscalChannel: Inflation affects nominal tax bases and indexed expenditure with different lags. Index-linked gilts use RPI, so this CPI observation is not their direct revaluation rate.

events.description: ONS reported financial-year borrowing below the previous year but above government expectations, and revised earlier monthly estimates. September's release is due to incorporate annual updates and classification decisions.
events.likelyFiscalChannel: Changes to receipts, spending and historical outturn affect the comparison with the March OBR profile; revisions should be distinguished from new-month surprises.

events.event: HMRC reported higher year-to-date cash receipts
events.description: HMRC recorded £322.7bn of tax and NIC receipts in April–July 2026, £19.1bn above the same period a year earlier. These are cash receipts, not the accrued ONS public-sector receipts measure.
events.likelyFiscalChannel: Cash collection informs the tax picture; timing differences and coverage prevent treating the HMRC total as the ONS receipts surprise.
